content.text: I can see the reimbursements table has columns for reimbursement amounts (`PRS_REM_MNT`, `FLT_REM_MNT`). I also notice there are columns `FLX_ANN_MOI` (appears to be year/month for care delivery), `SOI_ANN` and `SOI_MOI` (appears to be year/month for claim processing). Let me query the data to understand it better and get the total for January 2025:

input.sql:
SELECT 
  FLX_ANN_MOI,
  SOI_ANN,
  SOI_MOI,
  COUNT(*) as row_count,
  SUM(PRS_REM_MNT) as prs_rem_total,
  SUM(FLT_REM_MNT) as flt_rem_total
FROM ANALYTICS.MARTS.FCT_REIMBURSEMENTS
WHERE FLX_ANN_MOI IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY FLX_ANN_MOI, SOI_ANN, SOI_MOI
ORDER BY FLX_ANN_MOI DESC, SOI_ANN DESC, SOI_MOI DESC
LIMIT 20

content.text: Good! I can see that `FLX_ANN_MOI` represents the month of care delivery. Let me check what January 2025 would be:

input.sql:
SELECT 
  FLX_ANN_MOI,
  SUM(PRS_REM_MNT) as prs_rem_total,
  SUM(FLT_REM_MNT) as flt_rem_total,
  SUM(PRS_REM_MNT) + SUM(FLT_REM_MNT) as total_reimbursed
FROM ANALYTICS.MARTS.FCT_REIMBURSEMENTS
WHERE FLX_ANN_MOI = 202501
GROUP BY FLX_ANN_MOI

content.text: Perfect! I found the answer. The total amount reimbursed for care delivered in January 2025 (regardless of when the claims were processed) is **568,796,761.23**.

SELECT SUM(PRS_REM_MNT) + SUM(FLT_REM_MNT) as total_reimbursed
FROM ANALYTICS.MARTS.FCT_REIMBURSEMENTS
WHERE FLX_ANN_MOI = 202501
